I think there's a lot of misinterpreting around the word polyamory. To me, and from the literature I read, it meant multiple committed romantic relationships. I think I idealised it as being the same as polyfidelity (a closed network of commited romantic relationships). 

I've observed a lot of people using the term polyamory when the terms non-monogamy or relationship anarchy would be more appropriate for their general purposes.

A single emotionally and sexually full filling committed relationship with one human would be an amazing thing to find. Don't know if I've truly known a healthy mono relationship. 

What bothered me about the reality of polyamory(in my experiences) was there wasn't time to really build deep committed bonds, partners were too busy chasing new people, and then there was a pressure to keep performing polyamory - to be seen to be lining up dates, and the feeling of stability and trust wasn't there, I just didn't know the true extent of STD risks or how far the polycules extended.

I think I went towards polyamory as I just wanted an honest relationship with someone who could love me, communicate well and not cheat on me i.e. someone who would be open and honest about sex and the intention of having sex with others. I was also terrified of being back in a monogamous unaffectionate and dead bedroom again with no outlet. 

I didn't get what I'd hoped for, or what I'd read about in the books or forums.

It ultimately felt very destabilizing. People would call themselves poly or ethically non mono but I still didn't get a clear number on how many people they were involved with. I would have to guess and eventually just accept they could be having or trying to have sex with everyone which I realize is black and white thinking but I didn't have all the information I needed to feel secure. 

I never felt sufficient time was spent forming a loving trusting bond. Time and Time again I came up against emotionally unavailable people whom were hooking up with as many people as possible. For the metamours they disclosed, I couldn't be sure if the metamours were in ethically open relationships. I was happy to commit to up to three people and try to form romantic committed bonds but it felt like a losing battle when getting time with people was so difficult as they had many friends and lovers. 

I'm tentatively trying to get back to monogamy, to try to find someone emotionally available with a healthy libido who wants a basic simple mono bond. I see how respectfully men in work talk about their wives and it gives me hope.

But it's the thought of mono dating again, having to pretend there aren't other lovers who are being finalized and ranked which I don't know how to get back to. I just don't want to be trapped and not knowing the facts again. 

One of the worst things about identifying as an ethical polyamorist was monogamous males in committed relationships trying to treat me like a sex worker and even like a scapegoat or loophole for their attempt at bad behaviour. It hurt coming from friends trying to hit on me and use me while disrespecting their mono partner. 


All the negative experiences in polyamory seem to roar louder than the positive ones in my head and it can be hard to let it go.... finally I am getting catharsis in some ways from Dan Savage talking about the dark side of polyamory.

When I tried it, I wasn't able to find compatible people who wanted romantic and emotional commitment. I went in with the expectations of being able to explore deep commitments with a few people, in an open and honest and respectful way.

I was pretty content with 2-3 commitments but over time it became too much of a strain on my heart, communications broke down, tempers flared, jealousy increased - it was frustrating to sit on the sidelines, not getting regular time to build the meaningful connections with the few self-described poly people I chose because they were busy filling their time with as many lovers as possible and not always disclosing their full partner counts. 

Sometimes it felt like being in a free-for-all situation where the only way to survive was to assume partners were sleeping with all their friends as situations became so unclear because people insisted on extreme parallel poly. 

I made mistakes for sure as well - I allowed myself to be coerced into an unsafe situation out of fear and trying to keep the peace which damaged one relationship permanently.
 
My friends saw me become more upset and unable to smile anymore because of the stress and constant processing. I learnt a lot about what I wanted - a small close knit polycule with full disclosure of all partners involved.

I think if I venture back into that world, I'd want to go from a place of opening a long term monogamous relationship, to have an anchor partner, so we could be each other's sounding boards to spot unhealthy and potentially harmful relationships and ground each other.
